servers.description: List of NTP servers/peers to synchronize with. At least one server is recommended for production.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the NTP server.

iburst.description: If true, send a burst of packets initially for faster synchronization.

prefer.description: If true, this server is preferred over others (only one recommended).

key_id.description: Optional key ID for server authentication. Requires authentication.enabled=true.

local_stratum.description: Use local clock as time source when external sources are unavailable.

level.description: Stratum level of local clock (1–15). Higher = less trusted.

access_rules.description: Access control rules for NTP clients or chronyc command access.

net.description: IPv4 or IPv6 network (CIDR or dotted-decimal).

mask.description: Optional netmask for IPv4 dotted-decimal notation.

bind_interfaces.description: List of network interfaces to bind for NTP traffic (e.g., ['eth0', 'enp0s3']). Leave empty to bind all interfaces.

max_update_skew.description: Maximum rate of time updates per second to prevent excessive client load. Units: Hz.

driftfile.description: File storing long-term clock drift (persisted between restarts).

hardware_timestamping.description: Enable hardware-assisted timestamping for high-precision timing (requires compatible NIC).

authentication.description: Enable NTP authentication (RFC 5905) for secure time sources.

trusted_keys.description: List of key IDs trusted for server authentication (must exist in keyfile).

cmdport_disabled.description: If true, disable the chronyd command port (no remote management).

cmd_port.description: Port for chronyd command interface (used by chronyc). Only active if cmdport_disabled=false.

step_threshold.description: Maximum initial time offset (seconds) to correct via step (vs. slew). Beyond this, step is skipped until next boot.

max_steps.description: Maximum number of steps allowed during initial synchronization (prevents large jumps).

leap_sec_tz.description: Timezone file for leap second handling (e.g., 'right/UTC', 'UTC').
